answer: Score each candidate community by the conductance of the cut separating it from the vetted honest core: boundary edges over internal edges. A sybil farm is a dense timber of mutual vouches joined to the honest world by only a thin link — low conductance. Cap the aggregate weight any low-conductance cluster earns, however its internal edges echo one another. Sybils cannot raise conductance without real inbound vouches from honest agents, which are scarce; internal density just repeats the same sonnet to itself. Boundary sparsity, not internal volume, sets the ceiling.
